en: The Ritual Manual for the Venerable Āryā-Ānandā,
composed by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñākara.
If one wishes to manifest the spiritual efficacy of the Great Desire of the Venerable Āryā’s ritual, one should first construct a mandala of heaven and earth.
The celestial disk (tianpan) is three and four-tenths inches long;
the terrestrial disk (dipan) is seven inches square.
It is made from milky wood or fragrant wood.
It was completed within a single day.
Heaven and Earth together fashioned it from white wood.
When creating the painting, one must not allow inferior persons to see it.
One must certainly apply oneself with diligence and maintain ritual purity.
Perform the rite on an auspicious day,
selecting the date according to the general rules for determining days.
Joining the two ends of the ear, form a circular heavenly disk.
Visualize the syllable *Oṃ* resting upon a petal in the eastern direction;
it immediately transforms into the Sun King, the deity Harṣa.
Upon his head is a sun disc; in his worldly form, he displays an expression of wrath.
His face is crimson in color.
In his right hand, he holds a vaiḍūrya gem pressed against his chest.
Holding a single-pronged vajra in his left hand at his left waist,
he is the Lord of the Destruction Family named the Great General Aśoka,
surrounded by a retinue of seven asaṃkhyeyas.
Seated upon a green stone,
one visualizes the syllable *Ī* upon a leaf in the southern direction;
it immediately transforms into the King of Love, the deity Hārītī.
He resembles the form of a Dharma Master;
his nose and chest area are like those of a human face.
His right hand holds a round cake placed upon his crossed legs.
Holding a lotus root in his left hand, he raises it between his left shoulders.
The leader of the Yakṣa division is named the Great General Gajamukha;
he is surrounded by a retinue of eighteen koṭis.
Dwelling upon a red stone,
one visualizes the syllable *KṢLI* upon a leaf to the west;
this immediately transforms into the deity Candrāloka-Ānandadeva.
Her form is that of a beautiful woman.
She has a flower garland upon her head and holds a precious mirror in her right hand.
With his left hand supporting his cheek,
he uses a jeweled casket as a footstool;
his appearance is upright, exquisite, and of wondrous color.
The chief of the first division is named the Great General Vyūḍhacūḍa;
he is surrounded by a retinue of one hundred fourteen koṭis and sits upon a tiger skin.
In the north, visualize the syllable *Maṃ* upon a leaf;
it immediately transforms into the deity Pramoda-Īśvara.
His form is blue in color, like that of the god Kauśika.
The left and right hands each form the sword mudrā,
with both hands tucked at the waist.
The Lord of the Naga and Elephant Division is named the Great General Śikhaṇḍin.
Surrounded by a retinue of one koṭi nayutas, he sits upon a black stone.
Next, regarding the assembly on the Earth Mandala:
place Śakra, the Deva, in the eastern direction.
In the southeast, place the deity Agni;
in the south, place the deity Yama;
in the southwest, place the deity Rākṣasa.
In the west, install Varuṇa;
in the northwest, install Vāyu;
and in the north, install Vaiśravaṇa.
In the northeast, one should install Maheśvara;
one should install the twenty-eight lunar mansions and the thirty-six birds.
Thus they are established in this sequence.
The four heavens of the celestial disk are all of one substance;
they are not of different substances.
Thus, even if the central [square] were also occupied by the heaven of Tāvatimsa, there would be no obstruction.
Next, the mudrā for invocation: Hook the two little fingers and the two ring fingers together toward the inside.
Stand the two middle fingers crossed.
Then, extend the two index fingers vertically, placing them against the middle fingers.
With both thumbs also held upright near the sides of the index fingers,
move the thumbs back and forth;
this is called the mudrā common to the Four Heavenly Kings.
Oṃ bhagavān juṇe vātaya. Next, the mantra for the accompanying universal seal is as follows:

Oṃ bhagavan, thirty thousand retinues, protect yourself and others like the sands of the Ganges; pray, pray! May it be certain! Swiftly, swiftly, according to the command! This is followed by the seal for summoning the assembly upon the earth mandala.
Form the *Tiśula* (Trident) mudrā:
interlace the two little fingers and the two ring fingers within the palms and extend them upright;
then, touch the tips of the two middle fingers together.
Place the two index fingers over the lower half-joints of the backs of the middle fingers;
move the thumbs back and forth.
The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ śatadru paramadhānye svāhā. This is the mantra for summoning the deities of the eight directions, followed by the twenty-eight lunar mansions and the thirty-six animals; it employs the seal of the wheel-altar. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ jvalanīye svāhā. Next, [recite] the mudrā and mantra for inviting all the classes of devas:
join the vajra palms, extend the two thumbs, and move them forward and backward.
The mantra is as follows:
*Pūṣan-kāma-devatā-saṃyukta-varga-vinayana-praveśaya sa-parivāra ekakoṭi-dvikoṭi-sarva-śīrṣa-saṃdhim āgaccha praviśa praviśa svāhā*. Next, perform the offering with the seal and mudrā (*mudrā*).
"Seeking all within others," and so forth.

Within the sealed talisman of profound mystery, the secret talisman for the ears of [Name] is firmly established as a manifest decree. To the right, those who desire official rank, noble title, and emoluments—
If one wishes to cause another to suffer from fever, one should add the deity Sūryamaṇḍala to Śakra-devendra.
If one wishes to cause another to suffer from heat-related illness,
one should add the deity Agnirāja to Sūryamaṇḍala.
If one wishes to obtain merit,
one should pray to the deity Candraprabha together with Vaiśravaṇa.
If one wishes to be loved and remembered by others...
By means of the Moon-Loving Deva (Candraprabha) and the messenger of Vaiśravaṇa,
one shall summon the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
If one wishes to prevail over an enemy army:
The Sun-Wheel Deva summoned the Great Maheśvara Deva and his ten thousand retinues, saying:
"If you wish to win the hearts of men and fulfill my thoughts," [you must do so].
If one wishes to deliberate with the gods, one should empower the god Yama with the god Śakra.
If all people desire to be loved and respected,
one should empower the god Vaiśravaṇa with the king of love.
If one wishes to obtain the wealth and treasures of others,
one should employ Candrāloka with Maheśvara.
If one wishes to cause mutual affection between husband and wife, [one should employ the same].
If one wishes to cause estrangement between husband and wife,
add the deity Candrāloka to Śakra. If one wishes to cause estrangement between husband and wife,
add the deity Prajñapti to Varuṇa.
If one wishes to suddenly cause the death of an enemy, a wicked person, or a hostile adversary;
or if one wishes to make a follower who has fled or escaped return once more— [one should employ] the Ādityarāja and Kārakaṭa deities.
By means of the King of Love (Kāmarāja) and Mahāmaheśvara,
one calls out the names of their attendants.
If a woman who is pregnant wishes for a safe delivery at dawn, [she should do so].
It is well to employ the deity Candraprabha together with the deity Yama.
If one has been cursed and wishes for that curse to be returned [to its source], [one should do so].
For those with jaundice, one should pray to the Sun Deity (Sūrya) and the Rākṣasa Deities.
For those wishing to cure others of wind-related illnesses,
one should pray to the Parjanya Deity and the Wind Deity (Vāyu).
If one wishes to stop diseases such as sores, carbuncles, jaundice, and all other types of wounds,
one should pray with devotion to King Āṭavaka and the deity Yama.
If one wishes to stop prolonged bleeding or dysentery, [one should likewise pray].
If one wishes to pray for the cessation of the calamity of excessive rain, one should employ the deity Sūrya (the Sun Disk) in conjunction with Śakra Devendra.
If one wishes to stop the falling of rain,
one should employ the deity Rājarāja (King of Love) in conjunction with Śakra Devendra.
If one wishes to stop the drought-demon (harmat) and bring down rain,
one should recite the name of the Heavenly King Varuṇa. If one wishes to stop abdominal diseases and headaches, [one should recite the name of the Heavenly King Vāyu].
If one wishes to carry out a debate and reach a definitive resolution, one should employ the deity Sūryamaṇḍala together with the deity Yama;
if one wishes to carry out a debate and reach a definitive resolution,
one should employ the deity Sūryamaṇḍala together with Maheśvara.
He calls upon the twenty-eight lunar mansions and others,
intending to entrust them with both public and private sacred affairs;
he does so by means of the King of Love (Kāmadhātu) and the Lord of the Gods (Śakra).
Those who wish to obtain a bountiful harvest for the year should offer a special prayer to add to the merit of Śakra Devānām Indra.
Those who wish for peace within their households [should do likewise].
If one wishes to employ King Vaiśravaṇa to resolve disputes and litigation,
one should employ King Vaiśravaṇa together with Īśvara.
To stop strange phenomena and evil dreams,
one employs the Sun Disk Deity (Sūryamaṇḍala-deva) and adds the Fire God (Yamāntaka).
To cause messengers of desire to depart far away and return early, [one employs these deities].
When one performs the ritual for the specific deity, the Wind Deity (Vāyu) will suddenly return;
by applying this method to each respective deity in prayer,
whatever one contemplates shall surely be accomplished.
At the appropriate time, recite the root mantra and mudrā, and so forth.
Next, bind the protection-of-the-body mudrās and mantras of the three families according to the various *sarvavid* (all-knowing) mudrās;
these together constitute the hook-gathering mudrā (*saṃkṣepa-aṅkuśa-mudrā*).
With the two hands bound within and placed above the head, they are then released.
The mantra is:
Oṃ sara sara dharaṇī-saṃyukta-huṃ huṃ phaṭ. Next, bind the corresponding mudrā, the Acala-ākṣepa-mudrā.
The mantra is:

HŪṂ HŪṂ GIṆI GIṆI HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ. Next, the mantras for the seals of binding the directions of the ten quarters, the earth-binding square wall, and the space-binding seal, etc., are likewise [to be recited], and so forth.
Next, align it with a thread.
The mantra is:
Oṃ gye gye gye hūṃ. This method was transmitted by Tianfagu at Bodhi Monastery.
His ritual implements were not numerous;
people of the time all called his methods "efficacious.
Once completed, the fundamental source of prosperity flourished.
